body.title: fix: populate 'access' table for explicit access grants to read public repositories
body.body:
Fixes #14980.

The purpose of `applyMinVisibility` was to prevent entries in the `access` table which say "user-a can read repo-b" when repo-b is already public, and therefore anyone can read it.  (This logic was present in the `refreshAccesses` codepath when the access table write was refactored in #14243, but, it wasn't applied to all codepaths that wrote `access`.)  This behaviour isn't correct -- Forgejo relies on those records being present for the repo search behaviour on the user dashboard, and for methods like `GetRepoReaders` which "return all users that have explicit read access or higher to the repository".

`applyMinVisibility` has been removed from the access recalc, and an appropriate test added.

Note: no automatic recalculation of the `access` table has been included in this PR.  When users are affected, a team membership change (removal, addition) will be needed to correct the data.  An automatic migration is possible... but... would require cloning a significant amount of logic into a DB migration.  I'm not sure the functional impact is worth it.

body.title: fix(ui): keep issue list trailing items right-aligned when they wrap
body.body:
## Description

In issue lists, the trailing block (assignees, comment count, tracked time) is rendered at the left edge of its own line when the title and labels are long enough to fill the whole row. It should stay right-aligned like in rows where everything fits on one line.

`.flex-item-header` uses `flex-wrap: wrap`. When the title and labels fill the row, `.flex-item-trailing` wraps onto a new line. It has `flex-grow: 0`, so it sits at the start of that line and `justify-content: end` has no effect. The fix adds `margin-left: auto` to `.flex-item .flex-item-trailing`, which pushes it to the right in both cases.

The rule is in the shared `flex-list.css`, so it also applies to other lists that use `flex-item-trailing`. Rows where the trailing block does not wrap look the same as before.
